clue.text: Lively music from island company going round other islands

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples

indicators.note: going round says the company abbreviation encircles the islands abbreviation

parts.note: CI stands for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A firm sailing from one island around a group of others has some cheerful tunes playing.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriccio is a free, lively instrumental piece in classical music.

clue.text: Sound money used in store

indicators.note: Sound at the start signals that the money word is to be heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: cash is ready money

explanation.surface: Sensible savings are put away in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden hoard or stockpile kept for later use.

clue.text: Want to see place in SW France and Paris, perhaps

parts.note: Pau is a town in south-west France near the Pyrenees
Paris is an example of a city

explanation.surface: Someone longs to visit a town in south-west France and the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of scarcity or shortage; paucity is a smallness of supply.

clue.text: Landlord has private stronghold inside

indicators.note: inside says the stronghold word sits within the private word

parts.note: inner, as in one's inner thoughts, means private
a keep is the fortified central tower of a castle

explanation.surface: A property owner keeps a personal fortress within his estate.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlord of a pub or inn is its keeper.

clue.text: Give a bell to monks to start meeting

parts.note: to give someone a bell is British slang for phoning them, to call them
a body of monks forms a religious order

explanation.surface: Someone rings the monastery bell to summon the brothers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a bell' is everyday British slang for making a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair opens proceedings by calling the meeting to order.

clue.text: Stupid person starts off on all fours

indicators.note: starts off asks for the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A fool begins crawling about on hands and knees.
explanation.definitionFit: An oaf is a clumsy, dim-witted lout.

clue.text: It has little significance for a lawyer

definitions.text: It has little significance for a lawyer

parts.words: It has little significance for a lawyer
parts.note: in legal French the word for small means minor, as in a lesser jury or offence, so to a lawyer it literally signifies little

explanation.surface: Something is of minor importance in a legal matter.
explanation.definitionFit: In law the old French adjective for small marks lesser things, as in a minor jury or lesser offence.

clue.text: Eliminate parking on drive

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
drive as a noun, an inner compulsion, is an urge

explanation.surface: A motorist is told to clear the cars off the driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' suggests a driveway; here it is the inner impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge is to rid oneself of something, to clear it out.

clue.text: Wave alarming Japanese chap turning up in new suit

indicators.note: in says the turned chap goes inside the rearranged letters
new says the letters of suit are made anew in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue says the word for chap is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A frightening fellow from Japan surfaces in a fresh outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns SUIT into TSUI, and 'turning up' makes NAM from MAN, which goes 'in' it. The definition takes in 'alarming Japanese' since the word comes from Japanese.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge, destructive sea wave, a word borrowed from Japanese.

clue.text: Writer sees cutter entering river

indicators.note: entering says the cutter goes into the river

parts.note: the Tay is the longest river in Scotland
a hacker is someone who chops or cuts

explanation.surface: An author watches a boat called a cutter sail into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' looks like a small boat; it is one who hacks.
explanation.definitionFit: William Makepeace Thackeray was the Victorian novelist who wrote Vanity Fair.

clue.text: Our link with the French underground

definitions.text: Our link with the French underground

parts.words: Our link with the French underground
parts.note: reads like contact with the wartime French Resistance, but means the rail tunnel under the sea between Britain and France

explanation.surface: A British agent's contact in the French Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underground' suggests the Resistance; it is literally below ground, under the Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname for the Channel Tunnel, the rail connection running beneath the sea to France.

clue.text: Chemical symbols for a salt written the wrong way

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: written the wrong way says the salt is spelt backwards

parts.note: alum is a salt, a double sulphate used in dyeing

explanation.surface: A chemist has written a salt's notation back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical formula is the set of element symbols showing a compound's make-up.

clue.text: Remove some characters from hotel, ideally

indicators.note: some characters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ideally, a few letters should be dropped from the hotel sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To elide is to omit, especially a sound or syllable in speech.

clue.text: Consumer group's discussions

parts.note: reads like the deliberations of a shoppers' watchdog, but the consumers are diners eating together

explanation.surface: A consumer watchdog holds its talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumer group' suggests a body protecting shoppers; here it is people consuming a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Table talk is the informal conversation of people gathered at a meal.

clue.text: What can be achieved by third man in the field?

definitions.text: What can be achieved by third man in the field?

parts.words: What can be achieved by third man in the field?
parts.note: third man looks like the cricket fielding position, but means whoever comes third in a sporting contest

explanation.surface: A cricket question about what the fielder at third man can do.
explanation.walkthrough: Third man is a cricket fielding position behind the wicket on the off side; here it is the competitor finishing third in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: The award for third place in a competition is made of the alloy of copper and tin.

clue.text: Girl calmly ignoring the odds

indicators.note: ignoring the odds says to skip the odd-placed letters of calmly and keep the even ones

explanation.surface: A young woman coolly disregards the betting.
explanation.definitionFit: Amy is a female first name.

clue.text: The sort of handicap any golfer would love

definitions.text: The sort of handicap any golfer would love

parts.words: The sort of handicap any golfer would love
parts.note: handicap means a burden or millstone, yet the same word names a hole played three under par, which golfers dream of

explanation.surface: A golfer daydreams of the ideal handicap.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is both a burden (from Coleridge's Ancient Mariner) and a golf score of three under par on a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden is a handicap, and in golf the word names a score three strokes under par.

clue.text: Employed in office, one can do a lot, all the same

definitions.text: Employed in office, one can do a lot, all the same

parts.words: Employed in office, one can do a lot, all the same
parts.note: reads like praise of a versatile worker, but describes an office machine turning out many identical sheets

explanation.surface: Praise for a capable office worker who gets plenty done regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all the same' looks like 'nevertheless' but means identical copies.
explanation.definitionFit: An office duplicating machine produces many identical copies of a document.

clue.text: Power involved with his new title

indicators.note: involved, meaning tangled up, says the letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Authority comes with a new rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Title in law is the right of possession, legal proprietorship.

clue.text: Result of using loaf in addition — an arithmetical error?

definitions.text: Result of using loaf in addition — an arithmetical error?

parts.words: Result of using loaf in addition — an arithmetical error?
parts.note: loaf suggests using one's head to add up, but a tradesman's bonus loaf turns twelve into thirteen

explanation.surface: Someone using their loaf when adding up still gets the sum wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using loaf' is British slang for using one's head; here it is an extra loaf of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirteen, from the tradesman's practice of giving an extra loaf with twelve.

clue.text: Unofficial sort of cabinet room

definitions.meaning: an informal group of advisers to a leader, outside the official cabinet
the room where cooking is done

explanation.definitionFit: An unofficial circle of advisers is a kitchen cabinet, and the word also names the cooking room.

clue.text: Shrub in alcove

definitions.meaning: the laurel shrub whose leaves flavour cooking
a recess in a wall or a window recess

explanation.definitionFit: The word names the laurel bush and also a recess in a room, as in a window recess.

clue.text: European children filmed deer outside home

indicators.note: outside says the film deer surrounds the home word

parts.note: Bambi is the fawn of the Disney animated film
in means at home

explanation.surface: Kids watched the cartoon deer outside the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for babies or little children, so children of a European country.

clue.text: About time Meg rejected a rude word?

indicators.note: About says the turned name surrounds the time letter
rejected says the name is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: Meg is a short form of Margaret

explanation.surface: After a while Meg turned down a crude remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns MARGARET to TERAGRAM, and 'About' wraps it round T. The definition is a four-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of four letters, and a rude expression is often called a four-letter word.

clue.text: Marble path

definitions.meaning: a large playing marble, often made of alabaster

explanation.definitionFit: A choice glass ball in children's games has this name, as does a narrow passage between buildings.

clue.text: Character from Italian city associated with love

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital
love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A figure from an Italian city is linked with romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'associated with love' points at Shakespeare's lover, but love is just O.
explanation.definitionFit: A character from Shakespeare, the young lover of Juliet.

clue.text: Location of shooting attack

definitions.meaning: the beginning or assault of something, as an illness

explanation.definitionFit: During filming, actors are on set; and a start or assault, as of an illness, is its onset.

clue.text: Work hard with English writer to create tragic heroine

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
Elia was the pen name of the English essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A writer toils hard alongside an English author to create a doomed heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's beloved, who drowns, is a tragic heroine of Shakespeare.

clue.text: Lawn cut for churchman

parts.note: reads like a parish gardener mowing grass for the vicar, but lawn is fine linen cut into a priestly garment

explanation.surface: Someone mows the grass for the vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawn is a fine linen cloth, so the clue describes a linen garment cut for a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A white linen vestment worn by priests at mass.

clue.text: From voyage, had returned bringing Mexican plants

indicators.note: returned says the voyage word and the following word are both read backwards

parts.note: a sail is a voyage by boat
taken as written

explanation.surface: Back from a trip, someone brought flowers from Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses SAILHAD to give the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: These tuberous garden flowers are native to Mexico.

clue.text: How a boy might be called cheerful, say

definitions.text: How a boy might be called

indicators.note: say signals that the cheerful word is heard spoken

parts.note: a sunny disposition is cheerful

explanation.surface: A cheerful lad might be addressed as such.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal form of address to a young boy or younger man.

clue.text: Modern writer's delivery with purpose

parts.note: in cricket a ball is one delivery bowled
the point of something is its purpose

explanation.surface: A contemporary author's speech has a clear aim.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket each delivery by the bowler is a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen, a twentieth-century invention, is a writing instrument.
